key_insight: Combining machine learning-based nitrogen planning with grower-informed, in-season AI adaptation can reduce fertiliser use while maintaining winter wheat yield and grain quality.
engineering_relevance: Deployable decision-support systems need to adapt recommendations to weather, machinery availability and budget constraints, not just optimise fertiliser rates.
method: Derive baseline fertilisation plans from a machine learning-based nitrogen-response curve.
Use a large language model to adjust schedules during the season.
Incorporate grower input and operational constraints to keep recommendations executable.
evidence_signal: Long-term experiments showed low retrospective economic decision-loss; field trials and farm deployments matched standard-practice yields with less nitrogen, with adapted schedules also retaining grain quality standards.
watch_item: Evidence focuses on winter wheat in England; transferability to other crops and regions requires validation.
paper_title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
